Until a week or two ago, merging a PR to FLT would trigger a CI run which would typically succeed and would take about 1 and a quarter hours; that's 15 minutes to compile the project and run leanblueprint, and then one hour to run doc-gen. The finish was typically

ℹ [12152/12152] Built FLT/FLT:docs (70s)

Here is an example: https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/actions/runs/24966815094/job/73102935503 and here is a screenshot with timings.

Note that "compile blueprint and documentation" is all in one job but the blueprint is quick, it's making the docs which takes an hour.

One week ago, doc-gen would typically take 2 hours and would often fail, so I would have to rerun it. The error was

I asked about this in #FLT and was pointed to a fix involving going to github, selecting the "actions" tab, clicking on "caches" on the left under "management" and then manually deleting all the caches, and then rerunning the job. This would typically succeed, although now building the project was taking 3 hours instead of 1 hour 15 minutes.

A few days ago I cleared cache and CI failed again. I am reluctant to merge new PRs when CI is failing but on this particular day my entire working day was spent running CI and hence not merging anything (it failed once in the morning, once in the early afternoon, and then I reran it just before leaving work in the early evening but then I have to wait 3 hours to see if it succeeds).

In exasperation I disabled docgen, and I got a blissful CI green tick under 20 minutes later.

The next day Kim re-enabled docgen which is now apparently fixed (although it's only a matter of time before it breaks again, in my experience), and CI passed again with building FLT taking around 20 minutes and then docgen taking a world record 3 hours and finishing

ℹ [12156/12156] Built FLT/FLT:docs (79s)

(note we're back to 12000 rather than 8000).

Here is a link to doc-gen working first time but taking 3 hours https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/actions/runs/25478594418/job/74757556539 . I have no idea why (a) it broke and (b) why it now takes 3 hours not 1 to make docs.

Looking at https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/commits/main/ it seems that FLT#778, merged on April 27th, took 76 minutes. Then FLT#913 by @Marcelo Lynch was merged and docgen didn't run because it only changed a yaml file. And then FLT#914 (a very minor mathlib bump from April 23rd to April 28th, not changing the version of lean we're using or anything) suddenly took 3 hours.

Perhaps "doc-gen broke" and "doc-gen tripled in compile time" are two unrelated things? Not sure. But that's where we are now, and it's really inconvenient that building docs takes 3 hours. It's also really inconvenient clearing cache but perhaps that problem has now gone away.

My current instinct is to remove doc-gen from FLT completely and just run it once a week e.g. at the weekend, so I can go back to CI taking 20 minutes and always succeeding. Even if we get it back to 75 minutes this is still quite a long time. I can perhaps get Imperial to pay money to speed things up somehow but if "speed it up" means "get it from 3 hours to 2 hours" then it's not worth it.

Can someone who knows something about CI shed any light on what is going on?
This looks like an instance of https://github.com/leanprover-community/docgen-action/issues/28

Via its Mathlib dependency, FLT depends on plausible at rev 228b68381da38478a2cbac8a596b944a7c7c5c1c, while doc-gen4 at the v4.30.0-rc2 tag (which is what gets picked up by docgen-action) depends on plausible at rev 86210d4ad1b08b086d0bd638637a75246523dbb8.
The version mismatch invalidates the mathlib olean cache, and causes a rebuild of mathlib oleans (not just the docs) during the doc generation step.
https://github.com/leanprover/leansqlite/pull/30 eliminated the dependency skew problem. In future doc-gen4 releases, it should prevent this problem.
In the meantime, this workaround should avoid the problem: https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/pull/948
Have you validated that this resolves the issue? I'd be willing to overwrite the doc-gen tag for the current RC if it does.
We have successfully been using this workaround on Noperthedron and Sphere-Packing, though not at this exact mathlib revision
I could validate by updating Noperthedron to the same mathlib revision that FLT is using, and checking that CI still works well.

Kevin Buzzard said:

And then FLT#914 (a very minor mathlib bump from April 23rd to April 28th, not changing the version of lean we're using or anything) suddenly took 3 hours.

Indeed, this mathlib bump, from 6cc078933b86576c169521239b2e2f36889c5eca to 56770c871215f35a538e404d6cb72d870e6f600e, changed the plausible dependency from 86210d4ad1b08b086d0bd638637a75246523dbb8 to 293af9b2a383eed4d04d66b898d608d0a44b750f
the workaround seems to be functioning well on Noperthedron with mathlib updated to the same rev as FLT: https://github.com/jcreedcmu/Noperthedron/actions/runs/25503751265/job/74843540316

Okay, I bumped the v4.30.0-rc2 tag to one that carries along the updated dependencies from above. If docgen-action re-pins doc-gen every time it runs this should now hopefully propagate through the eco system automatically? Is that the case? @David Renshaw
I believe that should be the case. Let me experiment with Noperthedron...

Thank you very much for this explanation! I am happy to be a guinea pig. Let me know whether I should be merging FLT#948 or whether that is a step in the wrong direction and I should just wait for doc-gen to heal.
My understanding is if docgen-action behaves as expected it should already have healed
It seems likely to me that you won't have to do anything. I'll have data about how things look on Noperthedron in an hour or so (docs cache is rebuilding now).
I'll merge a PR in about 5 minutes and we'll see what happens. Thanks a lot!
I expect you'll see a ~1 hour docs rebuild on the first run, and then after that the builds will go down to ~15 minutes.
That's consistent with what I would expect as well
The docs build has always taken an hour for me because I "have" to build a huge chunk of mathlib docs as well as FLT docs -- are you saying that it will no longer take an hour?
docgen-action is supposed to cache the building of the mathlib docs at least. So that sounds like something is going wrong.
I confirm that the new v4.30.0-rc2 tag on doc-gen4 fixes the plausible version-skew problem, bringing CI times back into a reasonable range.
I did need to manually purge the Noperthedron Github actions cache to get the fully-efficient sub-15-minute builds.
However, I am still seeing this issue: https://github.com/leanprover-community/docgen-action/issues/33 (404 errors on project-specific docs pages after a cache hit)

FLT is back to 1h20 so many thanks for the quick diagnosis and fix!

I have not yet tested the "doc-gen will be even quicker if I don't bump mathlib" theory, because a lot of my FLT PRs are mathlib bumps right now, as I experiment with hopscotch #mathlib4 > hopscotch-action: auto-bump mathlib, detect breaking changes @ 💬 .
If you see 404's on FLT docs pages, then I recommend pulling in my workaround like this: https://github.com/jcreedcmu/Noperthedron/commit/f8f93d7a502f3bf912f6264dabb0e8da26e4899d
I'm not submitting a PR right now, because I'm kind of curious whether you will hit the problem or not.
(I'm unlikely to be looking at the FLT docs pages any time soon)

I'm not seeing any evidence of docgen being quicker if I don't bump mathlib. Example: I just merged FLT#952 (bumping mathlib) and then FLT#954 (not bumping mathlib) and docgen took an hour both times.
